findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This means a user must be both admin and owner to pass, so a normal team admin who is not an owner receives a 403 when trying to add guests. The permission should be `isTeamAdmin(...) || isTeamOwner(...)`, or a single helper should be used.

findings.title: Any booking attendee can add guests and trigger invites
findings.body: The handler grants access to any user whose email appears in `booking.attendees`. An attendee can call the mutation with arbitrary email addresses, which adds those addresses to the booking, updates the organizer's calendar through EventManager, and sends emails to the organizer and all attendees. This is an authorization expansion beyond the organizer/team-admin dashboard flow and enables attendee-driven invite/spam abuse. The permission should be restricted to the organizer and authorized team admins/owners unless attendee self-service is explicitly intended and protected.

findings.title: Guest email filtering is case-sensitive and does not dedupe input
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` compares raw guest emails against existing attendee emails and against `blacklistedGuestEmails`, which are lowercased. Because guest emails are not normalized/lowercased and the `guests` array itself is not deduped, an uppercase form of a blacklisted address bypasses the blacklist, and duplicate addresses in one request create duplicate attendee rows. The server must trim/lowercase and dedupe before filtering and inserting, independent of the client-side Zod uniqueness check.

findings.title: Email logic receives all requested guests instead of actually added guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original request array, not `uniqueGuests`. If the request contains a new guest plus an already-existing attendee, `uniqueGuests` excludes the existing attendee from insertion, but the email manager still sees that address in `newGuests` and sends that existing attendee `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a full booking confirmation) instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Pass `uniqueGuests` to the email sender.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the current session user's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: The handler builds `EventManager` from `ctx.user` via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `{ ...user, credentials }`. When a team admin/owner or attendee invokes the mutation, this attempts to update the organizer's calendar using the caller's credentials. That can fail or update the wrong account even though the guests have already been persisted in the database. It should load and use the booking organizer's credentials for the calendar operation.

findings.title: Guests are persisted before external calendar update can fail
findings.body: The Prisma update inserts the new attendees before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs. If the calendar update throws, the mutation fails and the caller sees an error, but the guest rows remain in the booking without the corresponding calendar update (and before any emails). This leaves booking data and external calendars inconsistent. The operation needs failure handling or a rollback path.

findings.title: New guest emails bypass disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally sends organizer/team-member and attendee emails and does not accept or check `EventTypeMetadata`. Unlike other send functions, event types configured with `disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `disableStandardEmails.all.attendee` still receive these guest-added emails. The function should accept event type metadata and respect the same host/attendee email-disable guards as the existing email flows.

findings.title: Invalid email state is not cleared on success or non-cancel close
findings.body: After a failed validation, `isInvalidEmail` is set to true, but the success handler closes the dialog and only resets `multiEmailValue`; it never calls `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`. Closing via the dialog's X/overlay also does not reset either state. Reopening the dialog can therefore show a stale validation error and stale email values. Reset the dialog state on both success and any close path.

findings.title: No tests cover the new add-guests mutation
findings.body: This adds a security-sensitive mutation with authorization, deduplication, blacklist filtering, calendar update, and email behavior, but no tests are included. At minimum, tests should cover organizer vs team admin vs attendee permissions, duplicate/blacklisted email filtering, passing only actually-added guests to the email sender, and the error path when the calendar update fails.
